seo.title: Best Cheap Eats in Chiang Mai (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Chiang Mai's top 12 cheap eats for 2026! From legendary Khao Soi to succulent pork leg rice and vibrant market stalls, find delicious local food without breaking the bank. Your ultimate guide to affordable dining in Northern Thailand.

hero.h1: 12 Best Cheap Eats in Chiang Mai
hero.subtitle: Chiang Mai is a paradise for budget travelers and foodies alike, offering an incredible array of delicious, authentic Northern Thai cuisine and street food that won't empty your wallet.

picks.name: Khao Soi Khun Yai
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This legendary street-side stall is synonymous with Chiang Mai's most famous dish, Khao Soi. Operating only for lunch, they serve up a rich, creamy coconut curry noodle soup with tender chicken or pork, topped with crispy fried noodles. The simple setup and bustling atmosphere add to its authentic charm, making it a must-visit for any food lover.
picks.whatToOrder: The classic Khao Soi Gai (chicken) or Khao Soi Moo (pork).
picks.insiderTip: Go early for lunch, as they often sell out by 1 PM. It's closed on Sundays.
picks.redditQuote: "Khao Soi Khun Yai is simply divine. The best Khao Soi I've had in Chiang Mai, hands down. That broth... unforgettable."

picks.name: Chang Phuak Pork Leg Rice (Khao Kha Moo Chang Phueak)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Famous for its 'Cowboy Hat Lady,' this iconic street food stall serves incredibly tender, slow-braised pork leg over rice, drenched in a rich, savory gravy. Open only in the evenings, the stall attracts both locals and tourists with its delicious, comforting flavors and the charismatic owner, making for a memorable street food experience.
picks.whatToOrder: Khao Kha Moo (Pork Leg Rice) with extra egg if you're feeling indulgent.
picks.insiderTip: Expect a queue, especially during peak dinner hours, but it moves quickly. Grab a seat at one of the plastic tables and soak in the night market atmosphere.
picks.redditQuote: "The Cowboy Hat Lady's Khao Kha Moo is a Chiang Mai institution. That pork just melts in your mouth, and the sauce is perfectly balanced. Don't skip it!"

picks.name: Huen Phen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: During the day, Huen Phen operates as a simple, affordable curry and rice shop. By night, it transforms into a beautifully decorated, traditional Lanna restaurant, offering an extensive menu of authentic Northern Thai dishes in a charming, antique-filled setting. While slightly pricier than street food, it offers exceptional value for the quality and ambiance.
picks.whatToOrder: Gaeng Hung Lay (Burmese-style pork curry), Sai Oua (Northern Thai sausage), Nam Prik Ong (pork and tomato chili dip).
picks.insiderTip: Visit during dinner for the full Lanna experience with the ornate decor and lighting. It's popular, so come earlier or be prepared for a short wait.
picks.redditQuote: "Huen Phen at night is magical. The food is incredible, especially the Hung Lay curry, and the atmosphere feels like stepping back in time. Worth every baht."

picks.name: SP Chicken
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Famed for its perfectly roasted Gai Yang (grilled chicken), SP Chicken is a local favorite. The chickens are slow-roasted over charcoal, resulting in incredibly juicy meat with crispy, flavorful skin. Pair it with sticky rice, a spicy Som Tum (papaya salad), and their tangy dipping sauces for a complete and satisfying meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Whole Roasted Chicken (Gai Yang), Sticky Rice, Som Tum Thai or Laos.
picks.insiderTip: It's a popular lunch spot, so it can get busy. Don't be shy about eating with your hands – it's part of the experience, especially with sticky rice.
picks.redditQuote: "SP Chicken's Gai Yang is consistently amazing. That smoky flavor and juicy meat, paired with a spicy som tum, is my perfect meal in Chiang Mai."

picks.name: Cherng Doi Roast Chicken (Gai Yang Cherng Doi)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Often touted as a rival to SP Chicken, Cherng Doi also specializes in succulent Gai Yang and a wide array of Isaan (Northeastern Thai) dishes. Their roast chicken is incredibly tender and aromatic, cooked with herbs and spices. The vibrant menu also includes various som tums, larb, and grilled pork neck, all bursting with bold flavors.
picks.whatToOrder: Roast Chicken (Gai Yang), Som Tum Pla Ra (fermented fish papaya salad for the adventurous), Moo Yang (grilled pork neck).
picks.insiderTip: It's a bit further out from the Old City but easily accessible by Grab. The spice levels can be intense, so ask for 'mai phet' (not spicy) if you're sensitive.
picks.redditQuote: "Cherng Doi's roast chicken is simply superior to SP in my opinion, especially with their amazing spicy dipping sauces. Plus, their som tum variety is insane."

picks.name: Jok Sompet
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Jok Sompet is a beloved local institution, especially popular for breakfast or a late-night snack. They serve 'Jok,' a warm and comforting rice porridge (congee) typically topped with minced pork, soft-boiled eggs, and crispy noodles. It's a simple yet incredibly satisfying dish, perfect for a gentle start to the day or a soothing meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Jok Moo (pork congee) with an egg and crispy dough stick (pa tong go).
picks.insiderTip: It's busiest in the mornings as a breakfast spot. You can add various toppings like ginger, spring onion, and a dash of white pepper to customize your bowl.
picks.redditQuote: "Jok Sompet hit the spot after a night out. The pork congee with all the fixings was exactly what I needed, cheap and incredibly comforting."

picks.name: Tong Tem Toh
picks.whyItMadeTheList: One of the most popular Northern Thai restaurants in Nimman, Tong Tem Toh consistently draws crowds for its authentic Lanna cuisine. The menu features a wide variety of dishes, from curries and stir-fries to grilled meats and chili dips, all prepared with fresh, local ingredients. It's an excellent place to sample many regional specialties.
picks.whatToOrder: A full 'Khan Tok' style meal with Khao Niao (sticky rice), Nam Prik Noom (green chili dip), Gaeng Hung Lay, and fried pork belly with chili.
picks.insiderTip: Expect a wait, especially during peak dinner times. They have a system where you take a number. It's best enjoyed with a group so you can order and share many different dishes.
picks.redditQuote: "Tong Tem Toh is a must-visit for Northern Thai food in Nimman. Everything we ordered was fantastic, and surprisingly affordable considering how popular it is."

picks.name: Anchan Vegetarian Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A long-standing favorite for vegetarian and vegan diners, Anchan offers a creative and flavorful menu of Thai dishes, all made with fresh, locally sourced vegetables and no meat or fish sauce. Their menu changes weekly, ensuring variety and seasonality. The cozy, upstairs setting provides a pleasant dining experience.
picks.whatToOrder: Their weekly curry special, Mango Sticky Rice, or the Vegetarian Khao Soi.
picks.insiderTip: Located upstairs in a small plaza, it can be a little tricky to find but is well worth the effort. Check their whiteboard for the day's specials.
picks.redditQuote: "Anchan is a vegetarian paradise. The food is so fresh and flavorful, even my meat-loving friends enjoyed it. The mango sticky rice is heavenly."

picks.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
picks.neighborhood: Fa Ham (north of the Old City)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Another top contender for Chiang Mai's best Khao Soi, Mae Sai is a humble, no-frills eatery cherished by locals. Their version features a slightly sweeter, richer curry broth, offering a distinct flavor profile from other famous Khao Soi spots. It's a genuine taste of local Chiang Mai without the tourist crowds.
picks.whatToOrder: Khao Soi Gai (chicken) or Khao Soi Nua (beef), which is a less common but delicious option here.
picks.insiderTip: It's a bit off the beaten path, so a Grab or songthaew is recommended. It's a busy lunch spot, often closing when they sell out, typically by 2 PM.
picks.redditQuote: "Khao Soi Mae Sai is my personal favorite. The broth has this incredible depth, and the beef version is just phenomenal. Super authentic."

picks.name: Paak Dang (Isaan Food)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While some dishes lean towards a higher price point for 'cheap eats,' Paak Dang offers fantastic value for its high-quality, authentic Isaan cuisine and a pleasant riverside setting. Specializing in spicy and sour flavors, their menu boasts fantastic grilled fish, various Som Tum salads, and flavorful curries that are perfect for sharing.
picks.whatToOrder: Som Tum Pla Krob (crispy fish papaya salad), Gai Yang (grilled chicken), Pla Pao (salt-crusted grilled fish, excellent for groups).
picks.insiderTip: Great for an evening meal by the river. The atmosphere is more relaxed and slightly upscale than street food, but the prices remain very reasonable for the quality. Book ahead for riverside tables.
picks.redditQuote: "Paak Dang is such a gem for Isaan food. The grilled fish is incredible, and their som tum is perfectly spicy. Good value for a nice riverside spot."

picks.name: Mr. Kai Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mr. Kai Restaurant is a no-frills, family-run eatery known for its extensive menu of classic Thai dishes at incredibly budget-friendly prices. It's a reliable spot for popular choices like Pad Thai, curries, and stir-fries, serving consistently good food in a casual, welcoming environment. Perfect for a quick, satisfying, and cheap meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Pad See Ew, Green Curry with Chicken, or the Spring Rolls.
picks.insiderTip: Portions are generous, so you can easily share or try multiple dishes without breaking the bank. It's a great fallback if you're in the Old City and just want good, honest Thai food.
picks.redditQuote: "Mr. Kai's is my go-to for a quick, cheap, and tasty meal in the Old City. The Pad See Ew is consistently good, and the staff are super friendly."

picks.name: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) Food Stalls
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Warorot Market, Chiang Mai's oldest and most vibrant market, is a treasure trove of cheap eats. Explore countless stalls offering everything from freshly made curries and noodle soups to traditional Northern Thai snacks, sweets, and fresh produce. It's a fantastic place to immerse yourself in local life and graze on a variety of delicious, budget-friendly treats.
picks.whatToOrder: Sai Oua (Northern Thai sausage), Kanom Krok (coconut pancakes), Khao Soi (from one of the many stalls), or fresh fruit shakes.
picks.insiderTip: Go in the morning for the freshest cooked food and local breakfast items. The market is bustling, so be prepared for crowds and enjoy the sensory overload.
picks.redditQuote: "Warorot Market is an absolute must-do for foodies on a budget. I literally ate my way through the market for like $5, trying so many amazing local snacks."

faq.question: Is it safe to eat street food in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Yes, generally it is very safe to eat street food in Chiang Mai. Look for stalls that are busy with locals, have a high turnover of food, and appear clean. Many vendors specialize in one or two dishes, perfecting them over years. Stick to cooked foods and drinks without ice if you're particularly cautious, but most places maintain good hygiene.

faq.question: What are the must-try local Northern Thai dishes?
faq.answer: You absolutely must try Khao Soi, the iconic creamy curry noodle soup. Other essential Northern Thai dishes include Gaeng Hung Lay (Burmese-style pork curry), Sai Oua (grilled herbal sausage), and Nam Prik Noom or Nam Prik Ong (green or pork chili dips served with fresh vegetables and pork rinds).

faq.question: Do I need to tip for cheap eats in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Tipping is not generally expected at street food stalls or small, local eateries in Chiang Mai, as service charges are not customary. However, if you receive exceptional service or particularly enjoy your meal, leaving a small tip of 20-50 THB (or rounding up) would be a kind gesture and is always appreciated.

faq.question: Are there good vegetarian or vegan options for cheap eats?
faq.answer: Chiang Mai is very vegetarian and vegan-friendly, even for cheap eats! Many local restaurants, like Anchan Vegetarian, cater specifically to plant-based diets. You'll also find vegetarian versions of popular dishes like Pad Thai, curries (ask for 'jay' or 'mangsawirat' and no fish sauce), and fresh fruit shakes at most markets and street stalls.

faq.question: What's the best way to get around to these cheap eats spots?
faq.answer: For most spots within the Old City, walking or renting a bicycle is ideal. For places further afield, using ride-hailing apps like Grab (similar to Uber) is convenient and affordable. Red songthaews (shared taxis) are also a cheap option; just tell the driver where you want to go and negotiate the fare.

faq.question: What is the typical price range for a cheap meal in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: A full, satisfying meal at a street food stall or local eatery in Chiang Mai typically ranges from 40-150 THB ($1.15-$4.30) per person, depending on what you order and if you include drinks. You can find delicious snacks for as little as 20 THB, making it incredibly affordable to eat well.

methodology: Our team of local foodies and experienced travel writers scoured Chiang Mai's bustling streets, markets, and hidden alleys to find the most delicious and value-for-money dining spots. We prioritized authentic local flavors, consistent quality, positive customer reviews, and a memorable experience, ensuring every recommendation offers an exceptional taste of Northern Thailand on a budget.
